data.hypothesis: The selected 32x33 scalar tile uses a 32x8 block. This candidate instead assigns each thread a 2x2 subtile in a 16x16 block, using float2 transfers for adjacent input columns and, after the shared-memory transpose, adjacent output columns. This changes thread ownership and vector grouping; it may reduce transfer instruction overhead, but the narrower lane groups and changed shared-memory access pattern could offset that benefit. Compare it with the measured scalar and four-adjacent-element variants rather than assuming it is faster.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this transpose, test thread ownership separately from shared-tile padding; these measurements are target-specific.
memory_lessons.claim: The prior padded scalar candidate measured 3.398 us over three n=1024 samples, while the prior padded four-adjacent-element ownership candidate measured 3.142 us over three samples. Both were recorded valid and correct; these results do not establish that vectorization alone caused the difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this distinct 2x2-per-thread ownership variant with the same correctness cases and repeated n=1024 run.

data.notes: Historical controller observations: the baseline was valid/correct at a 16.919 us mean (three n=1024 samples); the selected padded-scalar parent was valid/correct at 3.398 us; the padded four-adjacent-element variant was valid/correct at 3.142 us. No build, correctness run, or timing was executed for this new candidate here; its build, required-size correctness, and repeated complete-run timing at n=1024 remain for controller evaluation.
transformations: Replaced the 32x8 scalar-thread tile kernel with a 16x16 block whose threads each own a 2x2 input subtile.
Used float2 input loads and output stores around a padded 32x33 shared-memory tile, exchanging the tile orientation between coalesced load and store phases.
Kept the run entry point and allocation behavior, used size_t linear offsets, and performed no arithmetic on matrix values.
